theme: A blight sweeps a one-variety crop

then.title: Ireland’s Great Famine begins
then.hook: A fungus rots Ireland’s potatoes, and a country living on one crop starves.
then.text: In 1845 a blight caused by Phytophthora infestans began rotting Ireland’s potatoes, the main food of the rural poor, who relied heavily on a single variety, the Lumper. About one million people died and over a million emigrated.

now.title: A banana fungus reaches Latin America
now.hook: In August 2019 Colombia declared a national emergency after a soil fungus reached its banana farms.
now.text: Tropical Race 4, a strain of Panama disease, was confirmed on Colombian banana farms in 2019. About 99% of exported bananas are a single clone, the Cavendish, which has no resistance to it.

followed: Ireland’s population fell by about a fifth within a decade. In 1861 Anton de Bary showed that a microbe caused the blight, helping found the science of plant disease.

next.title: A pathogen hits a global staple
next.text: Around 2193, a new pathogen could sweep through a staple grown worldwide from a handful of genetic lines, forcing a rushed switch to new varieties.
next.watch: A few varieties covering most of a crop, fungal strains spreading in soil and seed, and warmer weather helping pathogens reach new regions.

breaks: In Ireland, poverty, land tenure and government policy turned a crop failure into mass death; losing the Cavendish would raise prices and hurt growers, not starve nations.

theme: A regime polishes its image with games

then.title: Nazi Germany hosts the Olympics
then.hook: Hitler opens the Olympics, and “Jews not welcome” signs vanish for the Games.
then.text: Nazi Germany staged the 1936 Games to look peaceful and tolerant. A record 49 nations came, the first Olympic torch relay ran from Greece, and boycott campaigns in several countries failed. Germany topped the medal table; Jesse Owens won four golds.

now.title: Qatar hosts the World Cup
now.hook: The first World Cup in the Arab world ends with Messi lifting the trophy in Doha.
now.text: Qatar spent an estimated $220 billion on the most expensive World Cup ever. Rights groups criticised the treatment of the migrant workers who built it, and critics called it sportswashing. Argentina beat France in the final.

followed: Leni Riefenstahl’s film Olympia carried the Games’ image abroad in 1938. Within three years Germany had invaded Poland, and the next two Olympics were cancelled.

next.title: A new power stages a global games
next.text: Around 2108, a state seeking respect might spend record sums on a world sporting event, while debate over its record follows the broadcast everywhere.
next.watch: Record bids from states facing criticism, state funds buying clubs and leagues, and governing bodies dropping rights conditions from hosting rules.

breaks: Nazi Germany was preparing a war and a genocide; Qatar is a small state seeking influence and security, and its tournament drew scrutiny that 1936 never faced.
